name: No For An Answer
label: Revelation
lede: Orange County's straight edge answer to New York: one six-song 7", a future Rage Against the Machine singer on drums for a spell, and a frontman who still calls it the most musically feeble thing any of them did.

eras.title: Not called Just Say No
eras.text: Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby had already made noise together in Carry Nation, a band O'Mahony later called the most gorilla thing he ever did. No For An Answer was the next try: songs from ex-Half Off bassist Jeff Boetto, and a message about more than just not drinking.

years.h: Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby start [[Carry Nation|1440aef1-030f-4364-99d9-76eb61d9aa19]]
years.p: Before No For An Answer, Dan O'Mahony and guitarist Gavin Oglesby form Carry Nation in Orange County. O'Mahony admits the musical chemistry was thin at first.

years.h: No For An Answer forms in Orange County
years.p: Bassist Jeff Boetto, ex-Half Off, arrives with songs. The band nearly calls itself Just Say No, then takes its name from a song aimed at group identities and straight edge's own critics.
years.xp:
Just Say No survived anyway, as the opening track of the band's first record. The first line-up had Dan O'Mahony singing, Gavin Oglesby on guitar, Casey Jones on drums and John Mastropaulo on bass alongside Jeff Boetto, who was gone by the end of 1987.

O'Mahony also ran Workshed Records in the late 1980s. His description of the business model: the band got 25 percent of the pressing, and no one made any money.

eras.title: Revelation goes west
eras.text: No For An Answer gave Revelation its first West Coast record and gave straight edge a California voice that growled instead of chanted. The drum stool, meanwhile, became a revolving door with some famous names going through it.

years.h: You Laugh 7", Revelation's first West Coast release · REV 6
years.p: Six songs, from Just Say No to About Face. The first pressing ran in two batches a week apart, 972 and 1,031 copies, identical white labels, the cover opening at the top.
years.xp:
The second pressing of 2,000 got silver labels and a cover that opened at the bottom. Some went to the band with no sleeves at all, 200 came in sleeves with an "I Spy" logo, and later copies used a live-photo sleeve.

When Revelation reissued it in 1997, the entire first pressing of the reissue had its labels on the wrong sides.

years.cap: No For An Answer · via Discogs
years.src: Wikipedia: No For An Answer · Wikipedia: Chris Bratton
years.h: Zack de la Rocha plays drums in No For An Answer
years.p: Casey Jones and John Mastropaulo leave in 1988. Wikipedia lists a young [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]], later of [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] and [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], among the drummers who followed, before [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]] settles in.
years.xp: 1988 ran through Zack de la Rocha, Quinn Mallard and Chris Bratton on drums, with Sterling Wilson taking over bass and Rob Hayworth briefly on guitar. Bratton stayed into 1989 and went on to [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]] and [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]].

years.h: No For An Answer on WABC-TV's skinhead news report
years.p: No For An Answer turn up in a 1988 WABC-TV news segment on skinheads. Dan O'Mahony rejected both the skinhead and straight edge labels, saying the band was about more than not taking drugs.

eras.title: Hawker, CBGB and the flyers at the door
eras.text: Dan O'Mahony wanted the message in as many hands as possible, so No For An Answer left Revelation for Hawker, the Roadrunner offshoot, and a bigger push. It got them a New York showcase, a protest outside it, and then the band was done.

years.src: No Echo: The Story of Hawker Records · No Echo: Dan O'Mahony
years.p: Hawker's John Bello says the album cost about $5,000. He heard Sheer Terror and Killing Time in Dan O'Mahony's voice, one of the first growls in hardcore.
years.xp:
Bello singled out Domino Principle and Rusty Pipes, and liked that it wasn't over-produced the way a lot of 1989 records were. The songs took on drinking, drugs and child abuse.

Dan O'Mahony explained the move from Revelation simply: if you had something to say, you had to get it to as many people as possible.

q: They didn't think that I was evil, they thought I was wrong.
years.src: No Echo: Dan O'Mahony · No Echo: The Story of Hawker Records
years.h: Born Against's crowd pickets No For An Answer's CBGB showcase
years.p: At Hawker's Free for All live-album showcase at CBGB, with [[Token Entry|535d0a8d-1f4c-4f0b-a384-b7d9fcadb7d3]], Wrecking Crew and Rest in Pieces, the [[Born Against|983825cd-4c25-45c5-adbb-3f9cdced6285]] and ABC No Rio crowd hands out flyers saying it isn't hardcore.
years.xp:
Inside, it was packed: John Bello puts the crowd at about 700 people in a 500-capacity room. The show became the Free for All live compilation.

Dan O'Mahony took the protest as an argument, not a vendetta.

years.h: Joe Foster plays one show, and No For An Answer ends
years.p: Future [[Ignite|4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc]] and [[Speak 714|843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635]] guitarist Joe Foster fills in for a single show in 1989. The band stops that year; Dan O'Mahony moves on to [[411|1d8b0619-dc78-4e25-b787-29ae6385c256]], whose This Isn't Me arrives in 1991.

eras.title: Back in print, labels backwards
eras.text: The band came back briefly in 1994, and the records came back with it: a CD pairing No For An Answer with Carry Nation, and a Revelation reissue of You Laugh with a pressing-plant mistake built in.

years.h: No For An Answer reunite for the first time
years.p: Five years after splitting, Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby bring No For An Answer back for a short 1994 reunion.

years.h: No For An Answer and [[Carry Nation|1440aef1-030f-4364-99d9-76eb61d9aa19]] share one CD
years.p: Cargo and Tacklebox pair A Thought Crusade with Carry Nation's Face The Nation, putting Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby's two '80s bands on one disc.

years.h: Revelation reissues You Laugh with the labels reversed
years.p: Revelation re-presses You Laugh as a 7". All 1,000 copies of the reissue's first run come back with side A's label on side B.

eras.title: Only for a cause
eras.text: The original rhythm section came back, a new 7" followed on TKO, and No For An Answer took its place at Revelation's 25th birthday. Dan O'Mahony, by then a spoken-word performer, activist and author, set his own terms for playing at all.

years.cap: No For An Answer · via Discogs
years.h: No For An Answer's original line-up reunites
years.p: Casey Jones and John Mastropaulo rejoin Dan O'Mahony and Gavin Oglesby. The same year O'Mahony starts doing spoken word with [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]] and [[Sam McPheeters|51e1e6b1-1498-4873-a3aa-351493cc7ee7]].

years.h: It Makes Me Sick, No For An Answer's first new music since 1989
years.p: The reunited No For An Answer release It Makes Me Sick on TKO Records, 22 years after A Thought Crusade.

years.h: No For An Answer play Revelation's 25th anniversary shows
years.p: No For An Answer are on the bill when Revelation Records celebrates 25 years with shows in California.

years.h: "Just Say No" live at Rev25, Pomona, 2012
yt: "Just Say No" live at Rev25, Pomona, 2012

years.h: You Laugh pressed on yellow and grey vinyl
years.p: Revelation re-presses No For An Answer's You Laugh again: 548 copies on opaque yellow and 550 on opaque grey.

q: the most musically feeble thing any of us did
years.h: Dan O'Mahony ranks No For An Answer below 411
years.p: Looking back for No Echo, Dan O'Mahony calls No For An Answer the weakest music any of them made but sincere in its message, and says [[411|1d8b0619-dc78-4e25-b787-29ae6385c256]] was the more important band.
years.xp:
O'Mahony was in straight edge from 1983 to 1990, seven years out of more than 35 in music, and says the obsession with it doesn't add up mathematically. No For An Answer hasn't played for pay in years; he won't do it without a cause behind the show.

Gavin Oglesby, who also played in [[Ignite|4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc]], went on to join O'Mahony in [[Done Dying|f17a4ac7-c333-4c13-8a23-886bc984a81e]].
